task_spec: SUBJECT: make the ice/breaker matchup views express the FULL cost of an encounter -- credits, the non-credit resources a breaker must also spend (power counters, virus counters, trashing a card), the stealth-sourcing constraint on credits, and the Corp's own additional rez costs -- so a pair that currently reads 'not computable' shows a real, complete answer.

scope: R/build-implementation.R (break-sub cost-form parsing, ice additional-cost parsing), R/views-matchups.R (cost model + matchup output columns), R/mod_lane_board.R (stat strip chips), R/mod_matchup_explorer.R (table columns), inst/sql/schema/implementation.sql, inst/shiny-app/www/netrunner.css
out-of-scope: rebuilding the sync image / promoting an implementation release -- production action, user's call
out-of-scope: the rules lineage (RULES_DISCLAIMER_CONFIRMED is FALSE); all costs here come from the implementation lineage
out-of-scope: modelling actual Runner/Corp credit pools or game state -- this prices one encounter, not a game

IN SCOPE (was out-of-scope, reversed 2026-08-29): breakers with MULTIPLE break-sub clauses. Penrose and Lobisomem span two ice subtypes each and only one is recorded, so 234 real pairings are absent from the matchup table -- and since PR #27 an absent pairing renders as a definite CANNOT BREAK. PR #28 added an interim guard (break_subtype_count) that suppresses the false negative; M-001 owns the real fix per DL-029, and the guard retires with it.
constraints: MUST: never fold a non-credit resource into a credit total -- no conversion rate exists (user decision: 'Credits + separate resource chips')
MUST: stealth credits stay INSIDE cost_to_break as credits, annotated separately -- the qualifier says where they are sourced, not that they are a different currency
MUST: honesty over coverage -- unknown stays NA with a status column naming the reason; never guess a plausible number
MUST: comments explain WHY, especially why something is NOT done; rejected alternatives documented at the point of decision
MUST: no non-ASCII bytes in R source outside comments -- use \uXXXX escapes (R CMD check warns)
MUST: run roxygen after any @export change (pkgload::load_all hides export mistakes; installed app then fails to boot)
MUST: tolerate a release built before new columns exist -- fill_missing_columns() pattern, since the sync image is built from a pinned package SHA and data/code deploy separately
MUST: bump spec_id when the matchup output gains columns (cache identity)
MUST NOT: pass a literal TRUE to a require_*() pre-ship gate; opening a gate is a human attestation
MUST NOT: paint controls over card art (corrected twice already)
SHOULD: parser tests use card bodies copied VERBATIM from the mtgred/netrunner tree, not paraphrased fixtures
SHOULD: keep the wireframe's visual language -- the strip is BREAK n / differential / badge at 240px
entry_points: R/build-implementation.R:breaker_economics() - matches (break-sub <int> <int> "Subtype") only; anything else returns parse_status='non_credit_break_cost' with the cost DISCARDED. 17 cards.
R/build-implementation.R:pump_economics() - written in step 1; the working model for parsing a cost form. break-sub parsing should mirror it.
R/build-implementation.R:ice_subroutine_count()/ice_parse_status() - where ice additional rez costs would be read from ice.clj
R/views-matchups.R:compute_cost_to_break_formula() - takes pump_resource_type and returns NA when a resource pump is needed; break-side equivalent needed
R/views-matchups.R:compute_ice_breaker_matchups() - assembles matchup output; emits cost_to_break, stealth_credits, credit_differential, source
R/mod_lane_board.R:stat_strip_ui() - renders BREAK n / differential / badge; where chips must go
R/mod_lane_board.R:assumed_pair_cost() - duplicates the formula call for overridden pairs; must stay in step with any signature change
rejected_alternatives: Full cost vector replacing cost_to_break - rejected by user; changes the lane board's whole visual language (wireframe strip assumes one number each)
Credits only, flag the rest incomplete - rejected by user; leaves misparsed breakers showing no cost at all
Filtering matchups by format at compute time - rejected in an earlier step; bakes format into manifest cache identity
Acquiring external Netrunner rules text - rejected: the implementation lineage already encodes every cost structurally; the rules lineage is gated closed and would not help (costs are card-specific)
Writing subtype overrides to matchup_overrides.csv - rejected in step 2; that file is for corrections true of the CARDS, not one board state
current_understanding: compute_ice_breaker_matchups() cross-joins ice x icebreakers, filters to subtype-compatible pairs via breaker_matches_ice(), prices each with compute_cost_to_break_formula(), merges matchup_overrides.csv, stamps source (formula/override/not_computable).

Cost taxonomy EXTRACTED FROM SOURCE (not recalled): inside break-sub/strength-pump the cost types are :credit (11, optionally qualified {:stealth 1} x10 or {:stealth :all-stealth} x8), :power (6), :trash-can (4), :virus (3), :trash-from-hand (3), :any-virus-counter (2), :trash-installed (1).

break-sub form shapes: (break-sub 1 ...) x70, (break-sub 2 ...) x31, (break-sub [(->c ...)]) x15, (break-sub nil ...) x5, (break-sub 0 ...) x4, (break-sub 3 ...) x3, (break-sub (->c ...)) x2, (break-sub cost ...) x1, (break-sub (:break-cost ...)) x1
Corp side: only 5 ice carry :additional-cost in ice.clj -- :tag-or-bad-pub x2, :forfeit x2, :derez-other-harmonic x1. Plus 3 bad-publicity references.

Step 1 (merged, PR #26) fixed strength-pump cost forms: 11 breakers were wrongly recorded as fixed-strength, making every stealth breaker report it could not reach ice it reaches routinely. Added pump_stealth/pump_resource_type/pump_resource_qty to traits and stealth_credits to the matchup table; spec_id -> v3.

Step 2 (merged, PR #27) split absent matchup rows into CANNOT BREAK (subtype filter excluded on purpose, overridable per lane) vs NOT COMPUTABLE (break_subtype NA, genuinely unknown). Added matchup_pair_state(), assumed_pair_cost(), override_control_ui().

AFTER step 1, still not_computable and blocked on BREAK-side parsing: Switchblade (break-sub (->c :credit 1 {:stealth 1}) 0 "Sentry"), Audrey v2, Faust. Blocked on resource CHIPS: Propeller (:power), Hantu (:virus + credits).

Step 1 is NOT LIVE: traits are built by the sync container from a pinned package SHA, so it takes effect only after an image rebuild + implementation re-sync. The app currently serves old traits and works correctly because of fill_missing_columns().
740 tests pass on master. Test suite runs only in the netrunner-mirror-sync:latest image with ENTRYPOINT overridden.

PR #28 (merged): break_sub_subtype() now takes the FIRST literal, since the subtype is the third positional argument -- this fixed Endless Hunger, which had recorded " subroutine" and so matched no ice and read as CANNOT BREAK against all 390. break_subtype_count added to traits and to the schema. Exactly 2 cards span >1 distinct subtype: Penrose and Lobisomem.

Paperclip RESOLVED: not a separate path; its (break-sub nil (cost-value eid :x-credits) "Barrier") is in its own defcard body at programs.clj:2569. A card is a variable-cost breaker only when it has NO fixed clause (DL-028) -- so only Paperclip and Matryoshka, not Lobisomem or Utae.
assumptions: break-sub cost forms use the same ->c grammar as strength-pump, so pump_economics()'s parsing generalises (H) -- verified for Switchblade/Audrey v2/Faust by reading source
(break-sub nil ...) x5 means 'no credit cost' rather than a parse failure (M) -- MUST be read from source before implementing, not assumed
(break-sub cost ...) and (break-sub (:break-cost ...)) are card-local bindings needing per-card reading, likely staying unreadable (M)
The 5 ice with :additional-cost cannot be priced in credits at all (tag/bad-pub/forfeit are not credits), so they become a Corp-side chip rather than a number folded into rez cost (H)
credit_differential stays rez_cost - cost_to_break and is NOT adjusted for non-credit costs on either side (H) -- a single subtraction stops being meaningful otherwise
Chips must appear in BOTH the lane board strip and the matchup explorer table, or the two views disagree about the same pair (H)
invisible_knowledge: not_computable is a first-class UI state, rendered explicitly (em dash, never a blank) -- a blank reads as 'zero cost', the opposite of what is meant
The distinction the whole codebase defends: 'you cannot do this' vs 'this is expensive' vs 'we do not know' are three different answers and must never collapse
A wrong answer wearing an honest NA's clothing is the worst outcome -- that was step 1's bug (breakers reporting they could not reach ice they reach routinely)
source badges mean provenance, not confidence: formula=derived, override=hand-curated, assumed=operator's premise + our arithmetic, cannot_break=definite negative, not_computable=unknown
The lane board lets the operator stack ANY breaker under ANY ice, so absent matchup rows are the common case there -- unlike the explorer, which only ever lists compatible pairs

assumed_pair_cost() in mod_lane_board.R re-implements the formula call for one pair; any change to compute_cost_to_break_formula()'s signature must be mirrored there or overridden pairs silently diverge from ordinary ones
matchup_overrides.csv is a header-only template in practice -- override handling must not assume rows exist
Comments in this codebase document rejected alternatives at the point of decision; matching that register is required or the file reads as foreign
